determinism.accounting: manifest bytes, object bytes, objects, JSON nodes, strings, dependency edges, replay calls, comparisons, and result bytes consume deterministic counters checked before corresponding work or allocation can exceed a declared bound
determinism.canonicalization: manifests and JSON objects use strict sorted compact UTF-8 JSON with one LF; object records and dependencies use fixed lexical order; binary checker inputs retain exact bytes; results use closed sorted compact ASCII JSON with one LF
determinism.identity: manifest SHA-256 addresses the committed bundle; every constituent is independently addressed by full SHA-256 and byte count; the replay result binds the manifest, complete inventory, fresh checker result, plugin version, contracts, implementation, configuration, inputs, and all foundation roles
determinism.platform: pure behavior depends only on exact bytes and declared CPython bytes, integer, tuple, dict, list, dataclass, JSON, Unicode NFC, and SHA-256 semantics, never on locale, default encoding, clock, host, checkout, environment, scheduling, hash iteration, or filesystem state
determinism.store: fan-out paths are objects/HH/remaining-digest and bundles/HH/remaining-digest/manifest.json; temporary names are non-semantic, writers are idempotent for identical bytes, and the manifest is the sole commit marker

effects.filesystem: replay_provenance_bundle performs none; the separately named provenance_store adapter uses only its caller-supplied root and creates content-addressed directories, temporary regular files, immutable objects, and an atomic manifest commit
effects.mutation: caller bytes and tuple are never mutated; returned values own immutable exact fields and all replay scratch state is local and discarded before return
effects.solver: none and no PySAT, Z3, SymPy, DPLL producer, discovery producer, router, MCP, CLI, clock, environment, randomness, dynamic import, or proof-assistant module is imported or executed by the pure verifier

ensures: replay_provenance_bundle is total over ordinary Python objects and returns one immutable verified, refuted, invalid, unsupported, or exhausted ProvenanceReplayResult without converting malformed input, producer output, stored verdicts, filenames, implementation defects, or partial work into mathematical authority.

Before interpreting an object, the verifier recomputes its byte count and full SHA-256, rejects duplicate supplied identities, proves exact manifest inventory equality, validates canonical JSON where declared, validates every contract and role binding, resolves the complete acyclic dependency graph, and checks the plugin identifier and version.

The verifier ignores the recorded checker verdict as authority, dispatches only the two allowlisted dependency-minimal checkers, reconstructs their request from exact input bytes, and compares the complete newly serialized checker result bytes to the recorded checker_result object.

A verified provenance result is issued only when the bundle is complete, every identity and cross-link matches, the fresh checker result is byte-identical to the recorded result, and that fresh checker returns verified with checker_attestation. The provenance layer preserves but never upgrades that authority.

A coherent, byte-identical replay whose fresh checker returns refuted, invalid, unsupported, or exhausted returns the same classified checker verdict with authority none; a malformed, partial, substituted, stale, mismatched, over-budget, unknown, or replay-divergent bundle returns invalid or exhausted with authority none.

Every result binds the exact manifest SHA-256, content-derived bundle SHA-256, object count, aggregate object bytes, checker identity, checker contract identity, fresh checker verdict and authority, fresh result SHA-256, completeness, exactness, stable reason and bounded diagnostic.

ProvenanceReplayResult has a closed public constructor, frozen slots, final subclass behavior, exact scalar fields, blocked pickle reduction, identity-preserving safe copying, canonical result bytes, full result SHA-256, and complete recomputation from retained manifest and object bytes at every validation or parse boundary.

The non-authoritative mathhead.provenance_store adapter may persist only a bundle that completed structural replay without invalid or exhausted provenance; it writes byte-verified objects before a manifest commit using atomic same-directory replacement, fsync where supported, and immutable fan-out paths derived solely from full SHA-256.

Store loading derives paths only from validated lowercase digests, refuses traversal, symlinks, non-regular files, multiple hard links, size drift, hash collisions, stale temporary state, missing or extra bundle objects, and replays the exact loaded bytes before returning a result. A failed or interrupted write leaves no committed manifest for a partial bundle.

mathhead.discovery.provenance retains its legacy proof_hash spelling only as an explicitly non-authoritative compatibility identifier and exposes the complete proof-term SHA-256 for migration; a 16-hex prefix can never identify a replay bundle or checker attestation.

The pure implementation remains within the MH-030 dependency-minimal closure of at most twelve internal modules and nine approved standard-library roots with zero third-party, denied, dynamic-import, discovery, transport, or effect roots.

epistemics.exhausted: the exact bundle is structurally supported but provenance validation or fresh checker replay cannot complete inside deterministic declared counters; no authority is issued and persistence is refused
epistemics.invalid: a type, encoding, schema, canonical form, identity, role, dependency, plugin, contract, implementation, configuration, inventory, recorded result, store object, or replay invariant is invalid or mismatched; no authority is issued
epistemics.refuted: the complete exact bundle replayed byte-identically and the fresh checker refuted or rejected its mathematical certificate; bundle_complete is true but mathematical authority is none
epistemics.unsupported: the complete exact bundle replayed byte-identically and its allowlisted checker reported a recognized unsupported format; bundle_complete is true but mathematical authority is none
epistemics.verified: the complete exact bundle passed every content and cross-link check and an allowlisted dependency-minimal checker freshly reproduced the exact recorded verified result with checker_attestation

invariants: Manifest object records are strictly ordered by role, have unique roles and unique content identities, and are exactly equal to the supplied object digest set; aliases, omissions, additions, and a digest assigned to multiple semantic roles are invalid.

All common role contracts, schemas, media types, and dependency sets are fixed. Proof dispatch requires only proof_term and SAT dispatch requires only cnf plus sat_certificate; objects for the other dispatch are forbidden rather than ignored.

problem_ir, theory_context, theory_plugin, resource_budget, evidence, certificate, engine_result, checker_result, checker_contract, checker_implementation, and checker_configuration are always present, content-addressed, and transitively bound into the manifest identity.

The checker contract object bytes equal the accepted artifact and its identity equals replay.checker_contract_sha256; implementation object bytes equal the allowlisted source basis; configuration bytes equal the checker-specific canonical configuration generated from accepted constants.

Proof replay parses only canonical mathhead.proof-term.v1 bytes and compares canonical mathhead.kernel-checker-result.v2 bytes from check_proof_term. SAT replay passes only exact canonical CNF and certificate bytes to check_sat_certificate and compares canonical mathhead.sat-replay-result.v1 bytes.

The recorded checker_result dependency set includes every semantic foundation role, certificate, dispatch input, checker contract, checker implementation, and checker configuration, so cross-run substitution cannot preserve the same manifest or result binding.

Producer labels, engine completion, Evidence or Certificate verdict fields, plugin claims, stored checker output, elapsed time, filenames, path casing, object constructor history, private-looking fields, object.__new__, object.__setattr__, copying, pickling, subclassing, shortened hashes, and compatibility adapters cannot mint checker_attestation.

Input byte, object, aggregate byte, node, nesting, string, dependency-edge, replay-call, logical-step, and result-byte ceilings are checked before corresponding parsing, allocation, traversal, replay, or output work; exhaustion never returns partial authority.
Filesystem persistence is never part of the trusted checker closure and never creates authority; every load repeats size, hash, manifest, dependency, and fresh checker replay checks from exact bytes.

The implementation imports only approved standard-library support and mathhead.kernel modules, carries exactly one top-level MH-C-PROVENANCE-REPLAY-001 ID and accepted SHA-256 binding, resolves the declared signature exactly, and imports no filesystem adapter, legacy provenance, producer, discovery, solver, or transport module.
The closed result envelope is governed by docs/contracts/schemas/provenance-replay-result-v1.schema.json=a40ac65f5d3560cb78be15ba121ba2d7e56c29c8d9f8abc2d10e4e8d07dcc4b0.

Store writes and loads reject absolute, dot, empty, mixed-case, non-hex, separator-bearing, symlinked, hard-linked, non-regular, wrong-owner-mode where enforceable, and resolved-outside-root components; no caller-controlled relative path is joined without digest derivation.
raises: Ordinary wrong types, malformed or noncanonical manifests, partial or mismatched inventories, invalid objects, unknown dispatches, checker disagreement, and deterministic resource exhaustion return classified non-authoritative ProvenanceReplayResult values rather than escaping as validation exceptions.

ProvenanceReplayValidationError with kind type, encoding, schema, canonical, duplicate, identity, result, or budget is raised only by explicitly requested result validation, hashing, serialization, or parse boundaries receiving forged, stale, malformed, noncanonical, or over-budget result data.

PermissionError is raised for direct public construction of replay result values; TypeError is raised for subclass and pickle attempts. The filesystem adapter raises classified ProvenanceStoreError for unsafe roots, paths, links, collisions, I/O failures, partial state, and bundles ineligible for persistence.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate and never yield a provenance result, committed manifest, object identity, or mathematical authority.

manifest is exact bytes no larger than 4194304 bytes and objects is an exact tuple containing exact bytes values only; text, bytearray, memoryview, path, stream, iterator, mapping, list, subclass, implicit coercion, and duplicate content identity are rejected by the authoritative boundary.

Manifest bytes are canonical UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, one LF, no duplicate keys, no BOM, no floats, no NUL, Unicode NFC strings, at most 64 levels, 4000000 nodes, and 1048576 code points per string, governed by docs/contracts/schemas/provenance-manifest-v1.schema.json=1c8be7ef43a42abf255e4799d60f2cccc8df05dfc82706f6de613fbf4f03776c.

A proof-term bundle has exactly the eleven common roles certificate, checker_configuration, checker_contract, checker_implementation, checker_result, engine_result, evidence, problem_ir, resource_budget, theory_context, theory_plugin plus proof_term; a SAT bundle has those common roles plus cnf and sat_certificate. Roles, object records, digest dependencies, and supplied object bytes each have one canonical order and identity.

Every object record fixes full lowercase SHA-256, exact positive byte count, media type, schema, governing contract identity or explicit null, and a sorted unique depends_on_sha256 list; all dependencies resolve inside the same bundle and the exact acyclic role graph required by this contract is present.

The theory_plugin object is canonical JSON with schema mathhead.theory-plugin.v1 and exact plugin_id and plugin_version equal to manifest.plugin; every other JSON foundation role has its contracted root schema and canonical bytes. Checker contract, implementation, configuration, inputs, and recorded result use their dispatch-specific exact schemas, bytes, and allowlisted identities.
